events.title: Juba I and the Pompeians destroy Curio's army on the Bagradas
events.description: In Caesar's Civil War, the Pompeians under Publius Attius Varus and King Juba I of Numidia routed the army of Caesar's general Gaius Scribonius Curio near the Bagradas River, in present-day Tunisia. Curio was killed in the battle.

events.title: Vesuvius erupts, burying Pompeii and Herculaneum
events.description: By the traditional date, Mount Vesuvius erupted and buried Pompeii and Herculaneum under ash and pumice, killing thousands. Some evidence suggests October; the ruins preserve a unique picture of Roman life.

events.title: Valentinian I makes his son Gratian co-Augustus
events.description: Emperor Valentinian I, who ruled the West while his brother Valens held the East, named his eldest son Gratian, aged eight, co-Augustus. Gratian inherited the West on his father's death in 375.

events.title: A priest at Philae carves the last known hieroglyphic inscription
events.description: In the temple of Philae in southern Egypt, the priest Nesmeterakhem carved a figure of the god Mandulis and a text hoping it would last "for all time and eternity". It is the last known ancient Egyptian inscription in Egyptian hieroglyphs.

events.title: Alaric's Visigoths sack Rome
events.description: The Visigoths under Alaric entered Rome and plundered it for three days, the first time the city had fallen to a foreign enemy in some 800 years. The shock prompted Augustine's City of God.

events.title: King John of England marries Isabella of Angoulême
events.description: King John of England married Isabella of Angoulême, heiress of the county of Angoulême, in Angoulême Cathedral. The marriage provoked the Lusignans and helped bring on John's loss of Normandy.

events.title: The earliest dated copy of the Gutenberg Bible is finished
events.description: The rubricator and binder Henricus Cremer finished his work on a copy of the Gutenberg Bible, the earliest dated copy known. The Bible was the earliest major book printed in Europe with mass-produced metal movable type.

events.title: Selim I defeats the Mamluk Sultanate at Marj Dabiq
events.description: Near Dabiq, 44 km north of Aleppo, the Ottoman army of Selim I defeated the Mamluk Sultanate. The victory gave Selim's armies control of the entire region of Syria and opened the door to the conquest of Egypt and the end of the Mamluk Sultanate.

events.title: British troops burn Washington
events.description: After routing American militia at Bladensburg, British forces entered Washington and set fire to the Capitol and the President's House. It was partly revenge for the American burning of York.

events.title: Amelia Earhart flies non-stop across the United States
events.description: Amelia Earhart flew from Los Angeles to Newark in about 19 hours, the first woman to cross the continent non-stop. That May she had become the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic.
events.html: Amelia Earhart flew from Los Angeles to Newark in about 19 hours, the first woman to cross the continent non-stop. That May she had become the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic.

events.title: Microsoft launches Windows 95
events.description: Microsoft released Windows 95 with a huge marketing campaign; customers queued at midnight. Its Start menu and taskbar set the pattern of the personal computer desktop for decades.
